finance.text: The US Federal Reserve kept its key rate unchanged and signalled patience as inflation cools.
finance.why: A pause keeps borrowing costs where they are for now, and signals the Fed sees inflation easing without needing tighter policy.
finance.impact: Steady rates tend to support stocks and bonds; the S&P 500 is down 1.20% on the day, so the pause has not lifted sentiment yet.

finance.text: Wall Street closed at a record high, with the S&P 500 up 0.8% on chip stocks.
finance.why: A record close shows investors are still willing to pay up for chip makers, which have led this year's gains.
finance.impact: Chip and tech shares carry the most weight here; strength in Asian tech suggests the rally is global rather than US-only.

finance.text: Brent crude rose 2% after producers extended output cuts.
finance.why: Extended output cuts keep supply tight, which feeds through to fuel prices and inflation.
finance.impact: Energy shares and oil exporters' currencies tend to benefit, while airlines and other fuel-heavy sectors face higher costs.

ai.text: Nvidia unveiled a data centre chip it says doubles training throughput.
The EU agreed rules requiring developers of general-purpose AI models to publish training data summaries.
A robotics start-up raised $400m for warehouse AI.
